cues.en: How's it going? Let's see if we can get my slide clicker out. Yeah, this is my first time in Singapore. Yeah, it's nice. Oh, this is already going well. If I get an applause for that, that's fantastic.
cues.zh: 进展怎么样？看看能不能把我的幻灯片翻页器拿出来。对，这是我第一次来新加坡。挺好。哦，这开场已经很顺利了。要是能因为这个得到掌声，那就太棒了。

cues.en: I haven't really looked around yet. I landed just before the conference, so I can't say I've really experienced it yet, but I'm going to stay on for a few days afterwards and have a proper explore. I brought my partner along with me as well, and I have to say that was a big mistake, a huge mistake. Because she's been really looking forward to this trip, right? And especially over the last couple of weeks, she's been saying things like, oh, I don't know, two weeks till we go to Singapore, one week till we go to Singapore, five days to go, four days to go. And I'm like, could you please?
cues.zh: 我还没怎么逛过。我是会议开始前才落地的，所以还谈不上真正体验过，不过会后我会再待几天，好好转转。我也把伴侣带来了，不得不说这是个重大错误，天大的错误。因为她特别期待这趟旅行，对吧？尤其过去几周，她一直在说，哦，不知道，还有两周就去新加坡了，还有一周就去新加坡了，还有五天，还有四天。我就想说，你能不能……

cues.en: not do that because what I'm hearing is five days, you only have five days to finish your talk, four days, three days, you're still not ready, are you? It's like the worst project manager ever just taunting me in how unprepared I am. She's brilliant because she knows how to put up with me because I stress, right? I stress pretty easily. I stress about things that aren't really problems. I stress about things that are really nothing to do with me.
cues.zh: 别这样了，因为我听到的是还有五天，你只剩五天来完成演讲，还有四天、三天，你还没准备好，是吧？就像史上最差的项目经理在嘲讽我有多没准备。她很厉害，因为她知道怎么忍受我，因为我会紧张，对吧？我很容易紧张。我会为一些根本不是问题的事情紧张。我会为一些跟我毫无关系的事情紧张。

cues.en: And someone posted this picture on Twitter last week. He's holding a MacBook between two fingers above concrete. I have not slept since I saw this picture. I stress about code like this, right? Firstly, because there's no semicolons. Give me a cheer if you use semicolons in JavaScript. Yes. Good to hear. The rest of you are monsters. But that's not the main thing that stresses me out. It's because it's adding stuff to the DOM.
cues.zh: 上周有人在Twitter上发了这张照片。他用两根手指夹着一台MacBook，悬在混凝土上方。我看到这张照片后就再没睡过。我会为这样的代码紧张，对吧？首先，因为没写分号。如果你在JavaScript里用分号，给我欢呼一下。是的。很高兴听到。你们剩下的人是怪物。但那不是让我紧张的主要原因。主要原因是它在往DOM里添加东西。

cues.en: and then hiding it, like presumably to show it some time later, like on click or something. And that stresses me out, because it's like, can we be sure that the user's not going to see a flash of that element before it's hidden? And I've never been able to recreate this problem. I've never seen it happen, but you never know when it comes to race conditions. So I'd always just swap those lines around, you know, just so I can get some sleep. But really...
cues.zh: 然后再把它隐藏起来，大概是想过一会儿再显示，比如点击的时候之类的。这让我很紧张，因为问题是，我们能确定用户在它被隐藏之前不会看到这个元素闪一下吗？我一直没能重现这个问题。我从没见过它发生，但说到竞态条件，你永远说不准。所以我总是会把那两行调换顺序，你知道，就为了能睡个觉。但说真的……

cues.en: There's no race condition here, because the timing of running code and rendering is all tightly defined and mostly deterministic. And that is thanks to the event loop. And if I do a half decent job in the next 30 or so minutes, you'll know why things run in the order they do. And I don't know. It might even make sense, but there's no promises there. So web pages have a thing that we tend to call the main thread.
cues.zh: 这里没有竞态条件，因为代码执行和渲染的时机都有严格定义，而且基本是确定性的。这要归功于事件循环。如果接下来30分钟左右我讲得还算像样，你就会明白为什么事情会按那个顺序运行。我也不知道。甚至可能讲得通，但我不打包票。网页有一个我们通常称为主线程的东西。

cues.en: Here's the main thread. We call it the main thread because loads of stuff happens here. It's where JavaScript happens. It's where rendering happens. It's where the DOM lives. And this means that the bulk of your stuff on the web has a deterministic order. And we don't get multiple bits of code running at the same time, like trying to edit the same DOM and giving you a world of horrible race conditions. But it does mean that if something on the main thread takes a long time,
cues.zh: 这是主线程。我们叫它主线程，因为大量的事情都发生在这里。JavaScript 在这里运行，渲染在这里进行，DOM 也住在这里。这意味着你在网页上的大部分操作都有一个确定的执行顺序。我们不会让多段代码同时运行，比如同时去编辑同一个 DOM，给你带来一堆可怕的竞态条件。但这也意味着，如果主线程上的某个东西耗时很长，

cues.en: And by a long time, I mean like 200 milliseconds. That's a long time in terms of user interaction. Then it becomes really noticeable because it's blocked loads of other things like it blocks rendering, it blocks interaction. And I think it's difficult for us to think in this way because as humans, we are extremely multi-threaded.
cues.zh: 所谓很长时间，我指的是比如 200 毫秒。就用户交互而言，这已经很长了。这时就会变得非常明显，因为它阻塞了很多其他事情，比如阻塞渲染、阻塞交互。我觉得我们很难这样去思考，因为作为人类，我们是高度多线程的。

cues.en: Like, I can stand here, I can wave one hand, I can stand on one leg, I can wave the other leg, and all the time I'm speaking, I'm breathing and processing audio and visual information. As humans, we don't really have a main thread. We don't really have things that block unrelated things. I mean, we have one, and that is when we sneeze. Because as you begin to sneeze, just stuff shuts down, you know? Like...
cues.zh: 比如，我可以站在这里，挥动一只手，单腿站立，再挥另一条腿，与此同时我还在讲话、呼吸、处理听觉和视觉信息。作为人类，我们并没有一个主线程，也没有什么会阻塞无关的事情。硬要说有的话，那就是打喷嚏了。因为当你开始要打喷嚏时，其他事情全都停摆了，你懂的，就像……

cues.en: And the first thing you lose is the ability to talk, then you pull a stupid face. If you're driving at this point, this is where you think, huh, I hope no one dies, at least of all me. And then the human body becomes entirely single-threaded, like you are sneezing, nothing else. You can't see, hear, think. You can move and make noises, but only in ways the sneeze wants you to. You have no control over this at all. And then it's over, right? You essentially wake up.
cues.zh: 你首先失去的是说话的能力，然后脸上会露出滑稽的表情。如果你这时候正在开车，你会想：呃，希望别有人出事，尤其是我自己。然后整个人体就完全变成单线程了，你就是在打喷嚏，其他什么都做不了。你看不见、听不到、也无法思考。你可以动、可以发出声音，但只能以喷嚏想要的方式。你对此完全没有控制权。然后喷嚏结束了，对吧？你基本上算是“醒了过来”。

cues.en: and you find out if your car is still on the road, if you have the same number of limbs you started with, the same number of passengers you started with. Needless to say, we don't want to write code that is like a sneeze. So although we have this main thread thing, we tend to spawn a whole series of threads, like for networking stuff, encoding and decoding, crypto, monitoring input devices.
cues.zh: 然后你发现车还在路上，四肢数量和开始时一样，乘客数量也没变。不用说，我们肯定不想写出像打喷嚏一样的代码。所以虽然我们有主线程这个东西，我们还是会派生出一整套线程，比如处理网络、编解码、加密、监听输入设备的线程。

cues.en: But once these threads have done something that the page needs to hear about, they need to sort of come back to the main thread to give it that information. And it's the event loop that orchestrates all of this. Take a set time out, for instance. Is it badly named? Yes. Are the arguments in the wrong order? I'd say so. But have you thought about how it actually works? Well, let's write a web standard for it, because that's what I do these days.
cues.zh: 但这些线程做了页面需要知道的事情之后，就得回到主线程，把信息交给它。而统筹协调这一切的，就是事件循环。拿 setTimeout 来说。它的名字起得糟糕吗？是的。参数顺序是不是反了？我也这么认为。但你有没有想过它到底是怎么工作的？那我们就来为它写一份 Web 标准吧，因为我现在干的就是这个。

cues.en: We'll start with a setTimeout method. When invoked, must run the following steps. Wait MS milliseconds, invoke callback. Done. But this isn't quite working. Because spec text, like this, this runs on the same thread as whatever invokes it. And in this case, it's invoked by JavaScript. So this is running on the main thread. So if we say, wait 5,000 milliseconds, we are waiting 5,000 milliseconds on the main thread. We're blocking lots of other stuff.
cues.zh: 我们将从 setTimeout 方法开始。调用时，必须执行以下步骤。等待 MS 毫秒，调用回调。完成。但这不太行。因为像这样的规范文本，运行在调用它的东西所在的同一个线程上。而这里，它是由 JavaScript 调用的。所以它运行在主线程上。所以如果我说等待 5,000 毫秒，我们就是在主线程上等 5,000 毫秒。我们阻塞了很多其他东西。

cues.en: So this spec is very sneezy right now, so we need to change that. And we do this. We run the steps in parallel, which is magic spec speak for get off the main thread, or get off this thread and run this stuff kind of at the same time as other stuff. But we created a new problem here, because now we're invoking a callback from something other than the main thread, and...
cues.zh: 所以这个规范现在太同步了，我们得改一下。我们这样做。我们并行执行这些步骤，这是规范里的魔法说法，意思是离开主线程，或者离开这个线程，让这些东西和其他东西差不多同时运行。但这里我们又制造了一个新问题，因为现在我们从主线程以外的东西调用回调，而且……

cues.en: I mean, there's no way this can really work. You would end up with lots of JavaScript running in parallel, still editing the same DOM, and you'd end up with all of these race conditions. So what we do is this. We queue a task, and we queue a task to get back onto the main thread at some point. And now we're calling JavaScript on the thread where JavaScript lives, so it all works. And this is a core part of how the browser works. If you click the mouse, how does that get from the operating system into your JavaScript? It queues a task.
cues.zh: 我是说，这根本不可能正常工作。你会得到大量并行运行的 JavaScript，还在编辑同一个 DOM，最后会出现各种竞态条件。所以我们这样做。我们排队一个任务，排一个任务，以便在某个时刻回到主线程。现在我们在 JavaScript 所在的线程上调用 JavaScript，所以就都正常了。这是浏览器工作方式的核心部分。你点击鼠标时，它怎么从操作系统进入你的 JavaScript？它会排队一个任务。

cues.en: When you fetch something, how do you get the response into your JavaScript? Well, it queues a task. And you send a message from a page to a worker. Once again, it queues a task to do that. So the first part of the event loop I want to look at are task queues. And this is the oldest part of the event loop. Rather than look at the spec, I thought it might be easier to try and visualize the event loop. So here it is. This is it. I hope that clears up any questions you have.
cues.zh: 当你 fetch 某个东西时，响应怎么进入你的 JavaScript？嗯，它会排队一个任务。你从一个页面给 worker 发消息。同样，它会为此排队一个任务。所以我想先看的事件循环第一部分是任务队列。这是事件循环最古老的部分。与其看规范，我觉得试着把事件循环可视化可能更容易。所以它在这里。就是这个。希望这能解答你们的疑问。

cues.en: Actually, I really hope it does, because I based the whole talk around this one diagram, so I hope it works. But yeah, without anything to do, the event loop just spins round and round in a CPU efficient manner. Now, this visualization is running at a fraction of a percent of real time, and it's still kind of too fast to really see what's going on. So let's slow things down a bit. When we queue a task, the event loop takes a detour. So this detour here, this is where tasks happen. So at some point, the browser says to the event loop, hey.
cues.zh: 实际上，我真的希望它能，因为整场演讲都围绕这一张图，所以我希望它有用。不过，没事可做时，事件循环就会以 CPU 高效的方式一圈一圈地转。现在，这个可视化只有实时速度的百分之零点几，但还是有点太快，看不清发生了什么。所以我们把它放慢一点。当我们排队一个任务时，事件循环会绕个弯。所以这里这个绕行，就是任务发生的地方。所以在某个时刻，浏览器对事件循环说，嘿。

cues.en: I've got a job for you to do, and the event loop is like, excellent, OK, add it to my to-do list, and I'll get round to it at some point. No problem, done. What if we do this? Using setTimeout, we queue two callbacks that we want to run after one second, 1,000 milliseconds. Well, according to the spec we wrote, these two algorithms go parallel. Each waits for 1,000 milliseconds, and then they need to come back onto the main thread, and they do that by queuing a task. So the browser sets the event loop.
cues.zh: 我有个活儿要你做，事件循环就说，太好了，好，加到我的待办列表里，我到时候会处理。没问题，搞定。如果我们这样做呢？用 setTimeout，我们排队两个回调，想在一秒后、也就是 1,000 毫秒后运行。那么，按照我们写的规范，这两个算法会并行。各自等待 1,000 毫秒，然后它们需要回到主线程，而它们通过排队一个任务来做到这点。于是浏览器就安排事件循环。

cues.en: Hey, I've got something here that wants to do main thread work. In fact, I have two things, and it adds each one as a separate to-do item in the task queue. Event loop's like, sure, that's fine, I'll get round to it. So it runs the first callback, it goes around the event loop, and runs the second callback. And that's tasks. And it would be pretty simple if that's all it was, but it gets more complicated when we think about the render steps.
cues.zh: 嘿，我这里有个东西想做主线程上的工作。实际上我有两个，它会把每个都作为独立待办项加到任务队列里。事件循环说，行吧，没问题，我回头处理。于是它运行第一个回调，绕事件循环一圈，再运行第二个回调。这就是任务。如果只是这样还挺简单，但当我们考虑渲染步骤时就更复杂了。

cues.en: And this is what the browser uses to update what's actually on the screen. The render steps are another detour, and that involves style calculation. This is looking at all of the CSS that's going on and working out what applies to each element, layouts, creating a render tree, figuring out where everything is on the page and where it's positioned, and then creating the actual pixel data, doing the actual painting. So at some point, the browser will say to the event loop, hey, we need to
cues.zh: 这是浏览器用来更新屏幕上实际内容的过程。渲染步骤是另一条绕路，涉及样式计算：查看所有 CSS，算出哪些样式应用到每个元素；布局：创建渲染树，确定页面上每个东西的位置和定位；然后生成实际的像素数据，真正进行绘制。所以某个时刻，浏览器会对事件循环说，嘿，我们需要

cues.en: We need to update what's on the screen. An event loop's like, no problem, I'll get round to that next time I go around the event loop. Now, I don't know about you, but I would consider myself an expert at coding badly. I can take very simple bits of JavaScript and create infinite loops out of them in places I least expect. But let's take a closer look at what happens when I do that. Here's a page with a gif and some text, and a big button that runs an infinite JavaScript loop.
cues.zh: 我们需要更新屏幕上的内容。事件循环说，没问题，我下次绕事件循环时再处理。我不知道你怎样，但我自认为很擅长写烂代码。我能拿非常简单的 JavaScript，在我最意想不到的地方搞出无限循环。但让我们仔细看看我这么做时会发生什么。这里有个页面，有 GIF、一些文本，还有一个大按钮，点击会运行一个无限 JavaScript 循环。

cues.en: So if I click that button, everything stops. The GIF has stopped. I can no longer select text. The whole tab has kind of come to a standstill. Code for this is simple. This is just button click while true. So how do we actually visualize this? Well, the user clicks the button, so the browser says, hey, event loop, I've got a task for you. Event loop's like, yep, no problem, I'm on it. But this task never ends. It's running JavaScript forever. A couple of milliseconds later, the browser says, hey, event loop.
cues.zh: 所以如果我点那个按钮，一切都会停下。GIF 停住了。我不能再选中文本。整个标签页有点陷入停滞。代码很简单，就是按钮点击后 while true。那我们要怎么把它可视化？用户点击按钮，浏览器就说，嘿，事件循环，我有个任务给你。事件循环说，好，没问题，我来处理。但这个任务永远不会结束，它在永远运行 JavaScript。几毫秒后，浏览器说，嘿，事件循环。

cues.en: We need to update that gif that was on the page. So if you could just render at your next earliest convenience, that would be fantastic. An event loop's like, yeah, okay, I'll get round to that right after I finish this infinite loop that I'm busy doing right now.
cues.zh: 我们需要更新页面上那个 GIF。所以如果你能在下次方便时尽早渲染，那就太好了。事件循环说，行吧，等我先忙完这个无限循环，就马上处理。

cues.en: Then the user tries to highlight text, and that involves like hit testing, it involves looking at the DOM to see what the text actually is, so the browser says, hey, I've got a couple more items for you to do list there, and the event looks like, are you having a laugh? Like, do you know how long it takes to perform an infinite loop? It's a long time, you know, there is a clue in the name.
cues.zh: 然后用户试图高亮文本，这涉及命中测试，涉及查看 DOM 来看文本到底是什么，所以浏览器说，嘿，我又有几项要加到你待办列表里。事件循环一副“你在开玩笑吗？”的样子，你知道执行一个无限循环要多久吗？很久的，你知道，名字里就有线索。

cues.en: So that is why a while loop blocks rendering and other page interaction. But this is a good thing in practice. We look again at the code that I started with. I used to worry that this would result in a flash of content, but it can't, right? Because this script runs as part of a task, and that must run to completion before the browser can get back around to the render steps. The event loop guarantees your task will complete before rendering next happens. It still stresses me out, though. I'll always swap these lines around when I see it in code.
cues.zh: 所以这就是为什么 while 循环会阻塞渲染和其他页面交互。但实践中这是好事。再看看我一开始用的代码。我以前担心这会导致内容闪烁，但不会，对吧？因为这段脚本作为任务的一部分运行，而任务必须运行完成，浏览器才能回到渲染步骤。事件循环保证你的任务会在下一次渲染发生前完成。不过这还是让我紧张。我在代码里看到它时，总会把这几行调换顺序。

cues.en: So, a while loop blocks rendering, but what about this? So this is a loop, but each time we go around the loop, we're using setTimeout to queue the next call. Well, let's find out. So, very similar tests from before. I clicked the button, and things are still working. In fact, it kind of looks like nothing's changed. But in the background, here's what's happening. We queue a task, go around the event loop, pick up that task, and we queue another task as a result. And that just...
cues.zh: 那么，while 循环会阻塞渲染，但这个呢？这是一个循环，但每次循环时，我们都用 setTimeout 排队下一次调用。那我们来试试看。测试和之前非常相似。我点击按钮，页面仍然正常。实际上，看起来好像什么都没变。但在后台，发生的是这样：我们排队一个任务，绕事件循环一圈，取出那个任务，然后作为结果又排队另一个任务。然后这就……

cues.en: keeps happening and happening until the end of time. But as we've already seen, only one task can be processed at a time. So when it's processed a task, it's having to go all the way around the event loop to pick up the next task. So that means that at some point the browser can say, huh, we should update the display for that GIF. And it can. It can go around and update the display. And that's why I said timeout loop is not render blocking. But if you want to run code that has anything to do with rendering,
cues.zh: 一直发生下去，直到永远。但正如我们已经看到的，一次只能处理一个任务。所以处理完一个任务后，它必须绕事件循环一整圈，才能取出下一个任务。这意味着浏览器在某个时刻可以说：嗯，我们该更新那个 GIF 的显示了。而它可以做到。它可以绕过去更新显示。这就是为什么我说 setTimeout 循环不会阻塞渲染。但如果你想运行任何与渲染有关的代码，

cues.en: A task is really the wrong place to do it, because a task is on the opposite side of the world to all of the rendering stuff as far as the event loop is concerned. What we want to do is we want to run code in the render steps. We want to run code here. And the browser lets us do that, and it lets us do that using requestAnimationFrame, another badly named function, I think. But it's really good for this purpose. Raph callbacks, they happen as part of the render steps.
cues.zh: 任务其实是错误的地方，因为就事件循环而言，任务和所有渲染相关的东西处在世界的两端。我们想要的是在渲染步骤中运行代码。我们想在这里运行代码。浏览器允许我们这样做，通过 requestAnimationFrame 做到，我觉得这又是一个名字起得不好的函数。但它非常适合这个用途。rAF 回调会作为渲染步骤的一部分发生。

cues.en: And to show why this is useful, I'm going to animate a box, just a box, and using this code. So I'm going to move that box forward one pixel, and then use RequestAnimationFrame to create a loop around this. And that's it. That's all it does. So that's RequestAnimationFrame. But what if we switch to RequestAnimationFrame for setTimeout? It looks like this.
cues.zh: 为了展示这为什么有用，我要让一个盒子动起来，就一个盒子，用这段代码。我会把那个盒子向前移动一个像素，然后用 requestAnimationFrame 围绕它创建一个循环。就这样。它只做这个。这就是 requestAnimationFrame。但如果我们把 setTimeout 换成 requestAnimationFrame 呢？看起来会是这样。

cues.en: This box is moving faster. It's moving about 3.5 times faster, and that means this callback is being called more often, and that is not a good thing. It's not a good thing at all. We saw earlier that the rendering can happen in between tasks. Yes, but just because it can happen doesn't mean it must. In reality, we can take a task. Should we render? No, can't be bothered yet. Go around the event loop, pick up another task. Should we render now? No, it doesn't feel like the right time. Many tasks can happen.
cues.zh: 这个盒子移动得更快。大约快了 3.5 倍，这意味着这个回调被调用得更频繁，而这不是好事。完全不是好事。我们之前看到，渲染可以发生在任务之间。是的，但能发生不代表必须发生。现实中，我们可以取出一个任务。要渲染吗？不，现在还懒得。绕事件循环一圈，取出另一个任务。现在要渲染吗？不，感觉时机不对。很多任务都可以发生。

cues.en: And before the browser goes, yeah, actually next time we will update the display. And the browser gets to decide when to do this. And it tries to be as efficient as possible. The render steps only happen if there's something actually worth updating. If nothing's changed, it won't bother. Like, if the browser tab is in the background, if it isn't visible, it will never run the render steps because there's no point.
cues.zh: 在浏览器继续之前，对，实际上下一次我们才会更新显示。浏览器可以决定什么时候做这件事。它会尽量高效。只有确实有值得更新的内容时，才会执行渲染步骤。如果什么都没变，它就不费这个劲。比如浏览器标签页在后台、不可见时，它永远不会执行渲染步骤，因为没意义。

cues.en: But also, the majority of screens update at a set frequency. In most cases, that's 60 times a second. Some screens go faster, some screens go slower. But 60 hertz is the most common. So if we change page styles like 1,000 times a second, it's not going to run the render steps 1,000 times a second. It will synchronize itself with the display and only render up to a frequency the display is capable of, usually 60 times a second. Otherwise, it would be a waste of time. There's no point rendering stuff the user will never see.
cues.zh: 但另外，大多数屏幕以固定频率更新。多数情况下是每秒 60 次。有些屏幕更快，有些更慢。但 60 赫兹最常见。所以如果我们每秒改 1000 次页面样式，它不会每秒执行 1000 次渲染步骤。它会与显示器同步，只以显示器能支持的频率渲染，通常是每秒 60 次。否则就是浪费时间。渲染用户永远看不到的东西没有意义。

cues.en: But that's what setTimeout is doing here. It's moving faster because it's updating the position of that box more times than the user can see. More times than this display is capable of showing us. Also, so far we've been using setTimeout as this kind of shorthand for a QR task, and it isn't really, because even though we've put zero milliseconds for the callback, it's more like 4.7 is what the browser will use as a default. The spec says the browser can pick any number to use, but in the things I've tested, it seems to be about 4.7.
cues.zh: 但这就是 setTimeout 在这里做的事。它跑得更快，因为它更新那个盒子位置的次数超过了用户能看到的次数。也超过了这块显示器能展示给我们的次数。另外，到目前为止我们一直把 setTimeout 当作排队任务的简写，但其实并不是，因为即使回调给的是 0 毫秒，浏览器实际默认更像 4.7。规范说浏览器可以选任意数字，但我测试的情况里，似乎是大约 4.7。

cues.en: There isn't a single method that just queues a task, but we can kind of fake it using message channels. And so I'd run a test with that. And if you're sensitive to flashing images, might be best to look away now, because that looks like this. There's so many tasks happening that it kind of just looks like the box is getting a random position. We're getting a task every 200th of a millisecond. So rendering can happen between tasks.
cues.zh: 没有一个方法能直接排队一个任务，但我们可以用消息通道来模拟。于是我用它跑了个测试。如果你对闪烁图像敏感，最好现在别看，因为看起来像这样。任务太多了，看起来就像盒子在随机跳位置。我们每 0.005 毫秒就得到一个任务。所以渲染可以发生在任务之间。

cues.en: but you can have many, even tens of thousands of tasks between renderings. Okay, flashing images are gone now. Let's imagine each of these is a frame that is displayed to the user, so our rendering steps, they happen at the start of each frame, and that includes style calculation, layout, and paint. Not necessarily all free every time, depends what actually needs updating. But I like this. I like this. This is very neat and tidy. This is a beautiful picture. Tasks, on the other hand,
cues.zh: 但两次渲染之间可以有很多任务，甚至数万个任务。好，闪烁图像没了。我们想象一下，这里每一个都是展示给用户的一帧，所以我们的渲染步骤发生在每一帧的开头，包括样式计算、布局和绘制。不一定每次三步都全做，取决于实际需要更新什么。但我喜欢这个。我喜欢这个。这非常整洁。这是一幅美丽的图景。另一方面，任务呢，

cues.en: They couldn't give us stuff. They just kind of appear anywhere they fancy. The event loop ensures that tasks appear, they happen in the right order, they happen in the order they were queued. But in terms of timing within a frame, there is no kind of ordering here at all. And we saw this with our set timeout. We were getting four per frame, three or four per frame. And that means that three quarters of those callbacks were wasted effort.
cues.zh: 它们做不到这一点。它们只是随意出现在任何地方。事件循环确保任务会出现、按正确顺序发生、按入队顺序发生。但就一帧内的时间安排而言，这里根本没有排序。我们在 setTimeout 里也看到了。我们每帧得到四个、三到四个。这意味着其中四分之三的回调都是白费功夫。

cues.en: in terms of rendering. Old animation libraries used to do something like this where they were trying to use a millisecond value that's going to give them roughly 60 callbacks per second. And they're assuming a lot about the screen there. They're assuming the screen's 60 hertz, but that was the common case. So it kind of worked. It eliminated some of the duplicate effort.
cues.zh: 在渲染方面。旧的动画库通常是这样做的：它们尝试用一个毫秒值来获得大约每秒 60 次回调。这里对屏幕做了很多假设。它们假设屏幕是 60 赫兹的，但这在当时是普遍情况。所以这勉强能用，也消除了一部分重复的工作。

cues.en: Unfortunately, it was a massive hack, because setTimeout is not designed for animation, and it really shows. Like, due to inaccuracies, you can end up with drift. So what's happened here is we're doing nothing in one frame, and then in the next frame, we're doing twice the amount of work. And that is a visual jank to user. It doesn't look great. Also, if one of your tasks runs long, you can end up moving the render steps around, because it's all running on the same thread, and you're sort of disturbing that lovely routine that they have. If we use requestAnimationFrame,
cues.zh: 遗憾的是，这是一个非常糟糕的黑客做法，因为 setTimeout 并不是为动画设计的，而且这一点非常明显。比如，由于计时不准确，你可能遇到漂移。这里的情况是：某一帧我们什么都没做，然后在下一帧，我们做了两倍的工作量。这对用户来说是视觉上的卡顿，看起来很不舒服。而且，如果某个任务运行时间过长，渲染步骤就可能会被挪动，因为它们都跑在同一个线程上，你会打乱浏览器那套优雅的固定流程。如果我们使用 requestAnimationFrame，

cues.en: Rather than set timeout, it would look a lot more like this, all neat and tidy, all nice and ordered. Everything is within the timing of the frame, even this longer task here. When I see performance traces like this, this makes me happy. This is showing a good user experience. It makes me feel very calm. You can't avoid tasks completely, of course, because...
cues.zh: 而不是 setTimeout，效果就会像这样，整洁有序、井井有条。所有事情都在帧的时间限制内完成，包括这个较长的任务。当我看到这样的性能轨迹时，我很开心。这表明用户体验良好，让我感到非常安心。当然，你不可能完全避开任务，因为……

cues.en: Things like click events are going to be delivered to you in the task, and generally you want to respond to those as soon as possible, fair enough. But if you have things like timers, or you have stuff coming from the network, I really recommend using RequestAnimationFrame to batch that work together, especially if you already have animations running, because you can save yourself a lot of duplicate work. I treat tasks like I treat people who drink fizzy water. I acknowledge that they exist, but I keep our interaction to a minimum because I do not trust them at all.
cues.zh: 像点击事件这类东西会通过任务传递给你，而且通常你希望尽快响应它们，这没问题。但如果你有一些定时器，或者有来自网络的数据，我真心建议用 requestAnimationFrame 把这些工作合并起来，尤其是当你已经有动画在跑的时候，因为这样可以省去大量重复的工作。我对任务的态度，就像我对喝气泡水的人的态度：我承认他们存在，但我会把和他们的接触降到最低，因为我完全不信他们。

cues.en: I mean, I would consider myself an empathetic person, but I have limits. I think soda water is totally disgusting, and I cannot think of a way that a human being could drink fizzy water without gagging or being sick or passing out or something. So people, when I say someone who does drink fizzy water, I think there must be something else going on with them. I maintain a Twitter list of people who drink fizzy water.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，我自认为是个有同理心的人，但也是有底线的。我觉得苏打水简直难喝至极，我想象不出一个人怎么能喝下气泡水而不干呕、不吐出来、不晕过去之类的。所以每当遇到喝气泡水的人，我就觉得他们肯定有什么别的问题。我专门维护了一个 Twitter 列表，记录那些喝气泡水的人。

cues.en: It's not a creepy thing. I just want to make sure I know what they're up to and what they're doing. But when I find the link between these people and Brexit and Donald Trump, I am blowing the case wide open, taking him straight to the FBI. And it pains me to tell you this, JSConf, but this conspiracy goes straight to the top. I saw him.
cues.zh: 这可不是什么偷窥行为。我只是想确保自己了解他们在搞什么名堂。而一旦我发现这些人和英国脱欧以及唐纳德·特朗普之间的关联，我就要把这个案子彻底揭开，直接报告给 FBI。JSConf，告诉你这些让我很痛心，但这个阴谋直通最高层。我亲眼看见他了。

cues.en: in an airport drinking fizzy water. Every now and then someone will say to me, it's like, oh, for Jake, you drink Diet Coke, and I think you'll find the main ingredient is fizzy water. No, that's different. That's completely different. Like, the main ingredient of air is nitrogen, right? But you would still die if that's all you breathed. So it's more like that. You cannot survive on just fizzy water. What was I talking about? Request animation frame. Right.
cues.zh: 我在机场喝气泡水。时不时有人跟我说，哦 Jake，你喝 Diet Coke，可你会发现主要成分就是气泡水。不，那不一样，完全不一样。就像空气的主要成分是氮气，对吧？但如果你只呼吸氮气，还是会死。所以更像是那样。你不能只靠气泡水活着。我刚说到哪儿了？requestAnimationFrame。对。

cues.en: There's one more detail I want to get to. And this is something that catches a lot of developers out. It caught me out. Request animation frame, it comes before processing CSS and before painting. So code like this might seem expensive, like we're showing and hiding a box many, many times. But this is actually really cheap. Like, JavaScript will always run to completion before rendering happens. So while you're doing this, the browser just sits back.
cues.zh: 还有一个细节我想讲。这个细节坑过很多开发者，也坑过我。requestAnimationFrame 在 CSS 处理和绘制之前执行。所以像这样的代码看起来可能开销很大，比如我们反复显示和隐藏一个盒子很多很多次。但实际上这非常便宜。因为 JavaScript 总会在渲染发生前运行完。所以你做这些的时候，浏览器就在旁边看着。

cues.en: and it lets you have your fun changing a value, and it doesn't really think about it in terms of CSS at all. And then at the end, when it actually comes round to the render steps, it goes, right, what did you actually change in the end? And the only bit that matters is this final line. And this explains a gotcha in CSS, or at least something that caught me out. I had a thing, right, that I wanted to animate from an exposition of 1000 to 500. And that sounds easy, right? So.
cues.zh: 它让你尽情改值，完全不会从 CSS 角度去考虑。然后到最后真正轮到渲染步骤时，它才想：好吧，你最终到底改了什么？真正重要的只有最后一行。这也解释了 CSS 里的一个坑，至少是坑过我的一个地方。我有个东西，想把它从 x 位置 1000 动画到 500。听起来很简单，对吧？于是。

cues.en: I had my listener here, I set the exposition to 1000, I told it to transition, and I changed the value to 500. But that animated from zero to 500, and I was like, that, come on browser, that's not, that isn't what I asked you to do, it's very clear, I said 1000 transition to 500 watts.
cues.zh: 我把监听器放这儿，把 x 位置设为 1000，告诉它做过渡，然后把值改成 500。但它却从 0 动画到 500。我当时就想，这也太……拜托浏览器，这不是我让你做的啊，很清楚，我说的是从 1000 过渡到 500。

cues.en: I figured out that maybe I'm giving it too much information all at once. And it's the same reason we saw before. The browser's not going to think about it, because I'm just in one block of JavaScript. So it's going to ignore that first transform value. So OK, fair enough. What I'll do then is I'm going to put this second bit. I'm going to put that inside a request animation frame. And now, it still animates from 0 to 500. And I was like, what is going on here?
cues.zh: 我明白了，也许我一次给它太多信息了。原因和之前看到的一样。浏览器不会去考虑，因为我还在一整块 JavaScript 里。所以它会忽略第一个 transform 值。好吧，行。那我接下来把第二部分放进一个 requestAnimationFrame 里。结果它还是从 0 动画到 500。我就想，这到底怎么回事？

cues.en: Well, I will tell you what's going on, because I finally figured it out. The user clicks on a button, and that's a task. So we come around to here. And this is where we set the initial transform and the transition. Fine. We cue an animation frame, and we go around. And this is where we set the destination, the final transform value. But the browser doesn't think about CSS until this next step over, the purple block there. This is where it calculates the CSS. So again,
cues.zh: 好，我告诉你怎么回事，因为我终于搞明白了。用户点击按钮，这是一个任务。于是我们转到这儿。这里我们设置初始 transform 和 transition。没问题。我们排入一个动画帧，然后继续转。这里我们设置目标值，也就是最终的 transform 值。但浏览器直到下一步，也就是那边的紫色块，才会考虑 CSS。这里才是它计算 CSS 的地方。所以又一次，

cues.en: It totally misses the first value because it hasn't thought about styles in between those two things being set. And that's why to make this work, you need to use not one, but two request animation frames. And now this will animate from 1,000 to 500. Incidentally, there is a hacky alternative to this. You can use something like getComputedStyle and just access one of the properties on it. And this forces the browser to perform style calculation a lot earlier than it naturally would.
cues.zh: 它完全漏掉第一个值，因为在这两个东西被设置之间，它没有考虑样式。所以要让它生效，你需要用的不是一个，而是两个 requestAnimationFrame。现在它就会从 1000 动画到 500。顺便说，还有个取巧的替代方案。你可以用 getComputedStyle 之类的，随便访问它的一个属性。这会迫使浏览器比自然情况下早得多地执行样式计算。

cues.en: But it makes the browser take note of all of the things you set up until that point. So it's like, oh, OK, transform translateX1000. That's a thing that this element does. But you need to be careful with doing this, because you can end up forcing the browser to do a lot of extra style work than it really wants to. It only really wants to do that once per frame. In reality, the best way to deal with this would be the animation API, the web animation API, because you can just say, I want it to go from here to this other value, and it all just works.
cues.zh:
但这会让浏览器记录下你到那时为止设置的所有内容。
于是它就像：“哦，好，transform translateX1000。”
这是这个元素会做的一件事。
但这样做要小心，因为你可能最终迫使浏览器做大量它并不想做的额外样式工作。
它实际上只想每帧做一次。
实际上，处理这个的最佳方式是动画 API，也就是 Web Animation API，因为你只要说“我想让它从这里变到这个值”，一切就都能正常工作。

cues.en: But that's only in Chrome, so it's not really worth talking about right now. So if the position of requestAnimationFrame within the render steps, if that was a surprise to you, if that was something you didn't know already, it's probably not your fault. You might have been misled by particular implementations, because Edge and Safari, they get this very wrong. They put Raph around about here. Most notably, they put it after paint.
cues.zh:
但这只在 Chrome 里支持，所以现在不太值得讨论。
所以，如果说 requestAnimationFrame 在渲染步骤中的位置让你感到意外，或者你之前并不知道这一点，那很可能不是你的错。
你可能被某些具体实现误导了，因为 Edge 和 Safari 在这件事上错得很离谱。
它们把 rAF 放在大概这里。
最明显的是，它们把它放在绘制之后。

cues.en: And that's kind of annoying, because it means that if the user clicks somewhere or something happens and you want to batch that work using RequestAnimationFrame, Edge and Safari, they will render before they get to your callback. So the user's going to see something. And that means that you're not going to see the actual changes you make until the next frame along. And that's adding quite a significant delay to things appearing on the screen. And it also makes it really difficult to batch work together.
cues.zh:
这有点烦人，因为这意味着如果用户点击了某处或发生了某件事，而你想用 RequestAnimationFrame 批量处理这些工作，Edge 和 Safari 会在执行到你的回调之前就进行渲染。
所以用户会先看到一些东西。
这意味着你做的实际改动要到下一帧才会显示出来。
这会给内容出现在屏幕上增加相当明显的延迟。
而且它也让把工作批量处理变得非常困难。

cues.en: I hope this is something to fix soon. There's been activity on the bugs recently. But the web standards say it should be here, and that's where it is in Firefox and in Chrome. OK, that's enough about RequestAnimationFrame. I want to take a look at microtasks. This is probably the least understood part of the event loop, I'd say. I strongly associate microtasks with promises. But this is not where they started.
cues.zh:
我希望这个问题能尽快修复。
最近这些 bug 上有些进展。
但 Web 标准规定它应该在这里，而 Firefox 和 Chrome 里它也确实在这里。
好了，关于 RequestAnimationFrame 就说到这里。
我想来看看微任务。
我想说，这大概是事件循环里最不被理解的部分。
我强烈地把微任务和 Promise 联系在一起。
但微任务并不是从这里开始的。

cues.en: Back in the 1990s, browsers wanted to give developers a way to monitor DOM changes. And the W3C went, OK, we'll sort that out for you. And they gave us mutation events. So this is where I can say, OK, I want to know when a node is inserted into the body element. And fine, excellent. And you get a series of other events as well. But in practice, this was pretty problematic. We take this bit of code here. What I'm doing is I'm adding 100 spans into the body element. How many events would you expect?
cues.zh:
早在 1990 年代，浏览器想给开发者一种监听 DOM 变化的方式。
W3C 就说：“好，我们来帮你解决。”
于是他们给了我们 mutation 事件。
所以这时我可以说：“好，我想知道什么时候有节点被插入 body 元素。”
好，太好了。
你还会得到一系列其他事件。
但在实践中，这问题很大。
我们拿这里这段代码来看。
我要做的是往 body 元素里添加 100 个 span。
你会预期收到多少个事件？

cues.en: to receive as a result of this. One event, one event for the whole operation? No. 100 events, one for each span? Yes. But also another 100 for this line here when the content is going into the actual span. A text node is going into the span. And because these events bubble, this simple piece of code is going to land you with 200 events.
cues.zh:
会因此收到多少？
一个事件，整个操作只触发一个事件？不。
100 个事件，每个 span 一个？对。
但这一行还会再产生 100 个事件，因为内容正被放进实际的 span 里。
一个文本节点正被放进 span 里。
而且因为这些事件会冒泡，这段简单的代码最终会让你收到 200 个事件。

cues.en: And because of this, relatively simple DOM modifications ended up triggering thousands of events. And if you were doing a tiny bit of work in these listeners, that quickly became a big bit of work, and it was a performance disaster. What we really wanted was a way to hear about a batch of this work. And similar to what we saw with styles before, we want the browser to sit back, let us do some stuff, and then at a convenient point say, some stuff changed. Here is an event or something to represent all of those changes.
cues.zh: 因此，相对简单的 DOM 修改最终会触发成千上万个事件。而如果你在这些监听器里只做一点点工作，这很快就会变成大量工作，性能会是一场灾难。我们真正想要的，是一种能一次性获知这一批工作的方式。就像之前样式那样，我们希望浏览器先放手，让我们做点事，然后在合适的时机说：有些东西变了。用一个事件之类的东西来表示所有这些变化。

cues.en: We want to hear about it once, not 200 times. And the answer became mutation observers, and they created a new queue called microtasks. A lot of documentation I read about microtasks suggests that it happens like, I don't know, every turn of the event loop, or it happens after a task, or something like that. And that is kind of true. There is a single place on the event loop where microtasks happen, but that is not where you'll generally encounter it. They also happen whenever JavaScript finishes executing.
cues.zh: 我们希望只听到一次，而不是 200 次。答案就是 MutationObserver，它创建了一个叫微任务的新队列。我读过的很多关于微任务的文档都暗示，它大概会在——我也说不准——事件循环每一轮发生时，或者在一个任务之后发生，诸如此类。这大致没错。事件循环上确实有一个执行微任务的单一位置，但那通常不是你遇到它的地方。每当 JavaScript 执行结束时，它们也会发生。

cues.en: And that means that the JavaScript stack has gone from having stuff in it to having no stuff in it. And that's where we run microtasks. So you can end up with microtasks happening halfway through a task. You can have microtasks in the render steps as part of request animation frames, kind of anywhere. Anywhere JavaScript can run. So that means this JavaScript will run to completion, adding 100 spams and their contents. JavaScript finishes executing, and we get our mutation observer callback.
cues.zh: 这就意味着 JavaScript 调用栈从有内容变成了空。而这就是我们运行微任务的时机。所以微任务可能在一个任务执行到一半时出现。微任务也可能出现在渲染步骤中，作为 requestAnimationFrame 的一部分，几乎在任何地方。只要 JavaScript 能运行的地方就行。也就是说，这段 JavaScript 会运行到结束，添加 100 个 spam 及其内容。JavaScript 执行完毕后，我们就会得到 mutation observer 回调。

cues.en: Promises made use of them as well, so here we queue a microtask, and then log yo. JavaScript is finished executing, so we go for the microtasks and we log hey. And that means when a promise callback is executing, you are guaranteed that no other JavaScript is midway through at the time. The promise callback is right at the bottom of the stack, and that's why promises use microtasks. But what happens if we create a loop using microtasks? A bit like we did with setTimeout before. Same demo again.
cues.zh: Promise 也用到了它们，所以这里我们入队一个微任务，然后打印 yo。JavaScript 执行完毕，于是我们处理微任务，并打印 hey。这意味着当 Promise 回调执行时，可以保证当时没有其他 JavaScript 正在执行到一半。Promise 回调正好位于调用栈底部，这就是 Promise 使用微任务的原因。但如果我们用微任务创建一个循环会发生什么？有点像之前用 setTimeout 做的那样。还是同一个演示。

cues.en: click the button, and it blocks rendering, it blocks the tab, in the same way a plain while loop did. Very different from set timeout before. So, promise callbacks are async, fine. But what does async actually mean? I mean, all it means is that they happen after synchronously executing code, so that's why we get yo before hey. But just being async doesn't mean it must yield to rendering, doesn't mean it must yield to any particular part of the event loop.
cues.zh: 点这个按钮会阻塞渲染，阻塞标签页，就像普通 while 循环那样。这和之前的 setTimeout 很不一样。所以，Promise 回调是异步的，没问题。但异步到底意味着什么？我的意思是，它只意味着这些回调会在同步代码执行完之后发生，所以我们才会先看到 yo 再看到 hey。但仅仅异步，并不意味着它必须让出给渲染，也不意味着它必须让出给事件循环中的某个特定部分。

cues.en: We've looked at three different queues so far. We looked at task queues, animation callback queues, which is where request animation frame callbacks happen, and now we're looking at micro tasks, and just to make your lives a little bit easier, they all are processed very subtly differently. Like we've seen with task queues, we take one item and we take one item only, and if another item is queued, it just goes to the end of the queue, fine. Animation callbacks, they happen until completion, except ones that were queued
cues.zh: 到目前为止，我们已经看了三种不同的队列。我们看了任务队列、动画回调队列——requestAnimationFrame 回调就在那里发生——现在我们在看微任务。为了让你们轻松一点，它们的处理方式其实都有非常细微的差别。就像我们在任务队列里看到的，我们取一个条目，而且只取一个；如果还有另一个条目被排队，它就只是排到队列末尾，没问题。动画回调会一直执行到完成，除了那些被排入队列的

cues.en: while we were processing animation callbacks. They are deferred to the next frame. Microtasks, on the other hand, they are processed to completion, including any additionally queued items. So if you are adding items to the queue as quickly as you're processing them, you are processing microtasks forever. The event loop cannot continue until that queue has completely emptied, and that is why it blocks rendering. Sorry, I get really excited about this stuff. I hope other people are excited about this as I am.
cues.zh:
当我们处理动画回调时。
它们会被推迟到下一帧。
另一方面，微任务会一直处理到完成，包括任何额外入队的项。
所以，如果你入队的速度和处理速度一样快，你就会永远处理微任务。
事件循环必须等这个队列完全清空才能继续，这就是它会阻塞渲染的原因。
抱歉，我对这些东西真的特别兴奋。
我希望其他人也能像我一样对此感到兴奋。

cues.en: I resolve the promise and then log something. But I have two event listeners on the same element doing the same thing. So if the user clicks a button, what happens in which order of things logged? Well, our first listener executes. Great, so that's on the JavaScript stack. Queues are micro-task, and then we get to the next line where we log listener one, and that is the first answer. Most folks agree on that bit, but what next?
cues.zh: 我 resolve 这个 Promise，然后记录点东西。但我在同一个元素上有两个事件监听器，做同样的事。那么如果用户点击按钮，会发生什么，记录的顺序是什么？好，我们的第一个监听器执行。很好，所以它在 JavaScript 栈上。排入微任务队列，然后我们到下一行，记录监听器一，这就是第一个答案。大多数人都同意这一点，但接下来呢？

cues.en: And I ran a Twitter poll on this last week. I've been speaking to a few of you. A few of you saw it. Most people would say the next thing logged is listener two. cues.en: So we've gone from having something on the JavaScript stack to nothing. So it is microtask time. We are going to run that promise, and we are going to log microtask one. And there we go. And then it's time for the second listener. And that works the same. So the order is listener one, microtask one, listener two, microtask two. But that's if the user clicks the button. What if the button is clicked using JavaScript? Oh, yes. It's different. For starters, our script is on the stack.
cues.zh: 所以我们从 JavaScript 栈上有东西，变成了什么都没有。所以现在是微任务时间。我们要运行那个 Promise，然后记录微任务一。然后就这样。接着轮到第二个监听器。它也一样。所以顺序是监听器一、微任务一、监听器二、微任务二。但那是用户点击按钮的情况。如果按钮是用 JavaScript 点击的呢？哦，对。那就不一样了。首先，我们的脚本在栈上。

cues.en: we call click and that synchronously dispatches the events. So we start with listener one, great. We queue a microtask and we log listener one. And now it's microtask time. No, no it is not microtask time. We can't run microtasks. This is where it's different because our JavaScript stack is not empty. Button.click has not returned yet. So we move on to listener two. We queue another microtask and now we log listener two. And this is where it diverges.
cues.zh: 我们调用 click，它会同步派发事件。于是从监听器一开始，很好。我们排入一个微任务，并打印 listener one。现在该处理微任务了。不，不，现在还不是处理微任务的时候。我们不能运行微任务。区别就在这里，因为我们的 JavaScript 调用栈还没清空。Button.click 还没有返回。于是继续到监听器二。我们再排入一个微任务，然后打印 listener two。分歧就出现在这里。

cues.en: And now our listener is done. In fact, all our listeners are done. Button.click returns our JavaScript stack to empties. And now we can process those microtasks, and they happen in order. And this has real world implications. So beware if you're using promises in this way, or if you're using automated tests as well. Because automated tests, if they're clicking things on the page, they're likely to be using JavaScript to do it. And that can change the behavior of your code.
cues.zh: 现在监听器执行完了。事实上，所有监听器都执行完了。Button.click 返回，JavaScript 调用栈清空。现在我们可以处理那些微任务了，它们会按顺序执行。这对现实场景有影响。所以如果你这样使用 Promise，或者也在用自动化测试，就要当心。因为自动化测试如果要点页面上的东西，很可能就是用 JavaScript 来点击。那会改变代码的行为。

cues.en: This also came up when we were looking at how to add observables to the DOM and how they'd integrate with promises. We hit this question. If we have a promise that represents the next click of a particular link, and it's just this little bit of code here, can someone use that promise and still call event.preventDefault? Promises are async, so have we missed our chance to prevent the default here? Turns out, no, it's fine. It's totally fine. This works. This just works. Unless, again,
cues.zh: 这个问题也出现在我们研究如何把 Observable 加到 DOM、以及它们如何与 Promise 集成的时候。我们遇到了这个问题。如果我们有一个 Promise 表示某个链接的下一次点击，而代码就是这里这一小段，那有人能用这个 Promise 的同时还调用 event.preventDefault 吗？Promise 是异步的，那我们是不是已经错过了阻止默认行为的机会？结果是没有，没问题。完全没问题。这能行。这就是能行。除非，又一次，

cues.en: the user clicks the link, or some code clicks the link using JavaScript. And this is the final puzzle of the talks, I'm overrunning a little bit. Has that event object's canceled flag been...
cues.zh: 用户点击了链接，或者某些代码用 JavaScript 点击了链接。这是本次演讲的最后一块拼图，我有点超时了。要弄清楚这一点，我们其实得看看规范。这是对点击链接的规范如何工作的非常粗略的描述。我们首先创建一个事件对象，然后对每个监听器，用这个事件对象调用它。接着我们检查那个对象。这个事件对象的 canceled 标志是否已经……

cues.en: If it's been set, then we're not going to follow the hyperlink. But if it's unset, we will follow the hyperlink. When you call event.preventDefault, it sets this cancel flag on the event object. So if a user clicks a link, that's fine. Our microtasks happen here after each callback, because that's where the JavaScript stack empties. But when we call click with JavaScript, it's just going to call out to our processor link click algorithm.
cues.zh: 如果它已被设置，我们就不会跟随超链接。但如果它未设置，我们就会跟随超链接。当你调用 event.preventDefault 时，它会在事件对象上设置这个取消标志。所以如果是用户点击链接，那没问题。我们的微任务会在每个回调之后发生，因为那里正是 JavaScript 调用栈清空的地方。但当我们用 JavaScript 调用 click 时，它只是去调用我们的链接点击处理算法。

cues.en: and it only returns once that algorithm is complete, so the JavaScript stack never empties during this algorithm, so our microtasks can't happen, so it hits this step three where it looks at the event object, and even if you've got loads of promises trying to call, like, prevent default, it's too late. It's gonna follow that hyperlink, and then sometime later, those promise callbacks happen, but you've missed the boat. You've missed the point where you can actually cancel that event.
cues.zh: 而它只会在该算法完成后才返回，所以在这个算法期间，JavaScript 调用栈永远不会清空，因此我们的微任务无法执行，于是它走到第三步，检查事件对象；即使你有一堆 Promise 想调用 preventDefault 之类的，也已经太晚了。它还是会跟随那个超链接，然后过一段时间，那些 Promise 回调才发生，但你已经错过时机了。你已经错过了真正能取消那个事件的时刻。
